office_does: The auditor runs Lewis County's elections and voter registration, records deeds and documents, and keeps the county's accounts and annual financial statement.
race_blurb: Open seat: Auditor Larry Grove is retiring. CPA Mitchell Merrill, endorsed by Grove and other county officials, finished 33 votes ahead of former county Republican Party chair Mitch Townsend in the primary. Townsend runs on auditing the voter rolls and every county department and on state election reform.

candidates.summary: Winlock-raised certified public accountant who owns Merrill CPA, P.S., running to keep the auditor's office accurate, transparent and professionally managed.
highlights: CPA with nearly 10 years in public accounting and an MBA from Pacific Lutheran University [S1][S3]
Promises to follow the law, use modern technology, widen access to information and build on his predecessor's work [S1]
Says elections must stay free from material error and fairly run [S1][S2]
Endorsed by Auditor Larry Grove, former Auditor Gary Zandell, Commissioners Brummer and Swope, the treasurer and the clerk [S2][S3]

experience.basis: First-time candidate, but runs as continuity with the retiring auditor, on professional credentials and with the backing of current and former county officials.

candidates.summary: Mossyrock School Board chair, former Lewis County Republican Party chair, Army infantry veteran and business owner running on a 'Contract with Lewis County' to audit the votes and open the books.
highlights: Would audit the voter rolls, using AI among other methods, and review every practice in the auditor's office within 30 days [S1][S2]
Promises a full financial re-examination of every county department [S1][S2][S4]
Backs voter ID with proof of citizenship, final results on election night and no late-arriving ballots [S3]
Says the job needs executive leadership, not a CPA [S1][S3]

spending.basis: Repeated, explicit platform of auditing the auditor's office and re-examining every county department's finances ('Audit and Open the Books').

reform.basis: Campaign centers on changing election rules through state election reform (voter ID, election-night results, ending late-arriving ballots), not on working within current practice.

experience.basis: Outsider to the office promising a top-to-bottom review to 'supercharge' it, though with long business, school-board and party leadership.
